original.title: Whose culture has capital? A critical race theory discussion of community cultural wealth

core_idea: Deficit views say marginalised students lack the 'right' cultural capital. Yosso argues their communities hold six forms of capital: aspirational, linguistic, familial, social, navigational and resistant.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How do first-generation, migrant or minority students draw on their communities to navigate education?
Which forms of capital help students persist?
Typical data: interviews, narrative inquiry, focus groups.
common_mistakes: Using the six capitals as a checklist to code anything positive.
Forgetting the CRT basis and using it as a generic 'strengths' frame.
Measuring the capitals with ad hoc survey items without validation.
